teachers.metaDescription: Build an interactive lesson for your students in minutes: in the studio, or with your own Claude or ChatGPT. Review it, publish it by link, and follow along.
teachers.title: Build an interactive lesson for your students in minutes.
teachers.lead: From your handout or an idea in your head: a board that draws itself in front of your students, a question after each idea, and Nova explaining by voice. You review and publish; your students open a link.
teachers.studioLead: Four steps, without writing a line of code.

studio.title: Type your idea or upload your handout
studio.text: A topic, a PDF or photos from the textbook. Say who the lesson is for and pick one of the ready-made looks.

studio.title: Watch it being built
studio.text: The lesson builds step by step in a few minutes, and you see each board as soon as it's drawn.

studio.title: Review and leave notes
studio.text: Open the lesson the way a student will see it and leave a note on any step. The fix lands right on that step.

studio.title: Publish by link and follow along
studio.text: One link for your students. See who started and who finished each lesson, and publish a new version whenever you make changes.

teachers.connectTitle: Option two: with your own Claude or ChatGPT
teachers.connectLead: If you like working with your own AI, connect it to the site and it writes the lesson right here. We check the format and save it as a draft in your account.

connect.title: In Claude, open Settings, then Connectors, then Add custom connector.
connect.text: Name it New Learn, with this URL:

connect.title: Log in to New Learn and allow the app.
connect.text: What it can do: create drafts and read your notes, nothing more. It can't publish or see your students.

connect.title: Ask for the lesson in your own words.
connect.text: For example: “Make me a lesson on compound interest for first-year business students, 3 scenes, in plain English.” It will ask you a few questions first and agree on a plan with you.

connect.title: Open the preview link it sends you.
connect.text: Leave notes on the steps, then tell it “Fix my notes.” When you're happy with it, publish it from the teacher dashboard.

teachers.chatgpt: In ChatGPT it works the same way, from Settings then Connectors, if your plan supports custom connectors.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: What New Learn stores, who sees it, and what reaches the AI.
privacy.intro: We write this as plainly as we'd like to read it ourselves. If anything is unclear, email us.

sections.title: What we store
bullets: Your account: your name, email and an encrypted password, through the Neon Auth service.
Your learning: the lessons you opened, where you stopped, and your answers to questions.
If you're a teacher: your courses, lessons, notes and boards, plus the courses you published and who enrolled in them.
Files you upload to build a lesson (a handout, images, text): stored temporarily until the lesson is built, then deleted.
Your settings, such as lesson speed, how questions work and the site language.

sections.title: Who sees it
bullets: You, from your account.
The teacher who made a course sees how many people started and finished each lesson, but not your detailed answers.
Students see the teacher's name on the course.
Our team, only when needed, to fix a problem or answer a support request.
We don't sell your data or give it to anyone for advertising.

sections.title: AI
bullets: Nova, the lesson assistant, runs on Google Gemini models. We send it the current step of the lesson and your question, plus your voice if you turn voice on. The conversation is sent to the model so it can reply, and we don't use it to train models.
Lesson building uses Anthropic models (Claude): we send the idea you wrote and the files you uploaded so it can write the lesson.

If you connect your own Claude or ChatGPT to the site, it sees only your drafts and notes, with the access you approved, and it can't publish or see students. You can revoke the connection by emailing us.
Lessons written by AI are labeled as such on the platform, and they can contain mistakes; the teacher reviews them before publishing.

sections.title: Cookies and tracking
paragraphs: We use a single session cookie to keep you logged in, and the site language you choose is saved on your device. There are no ads, no trackers, and no analytics that identify you.

sections.title: Where your data lives
paragraphs: The site runs on Cloudflare and the database on Neon. The boards a lesson draws run in an isolated page with no access to your account.

sections.title: Children
paragraphs: Accounts are for people aged 13 or older. Younger children use the platform through a parent's or the school's account, and the parent or guardian is responsible for that account.

sections.title: Deleting your account
paragraphs: Email us from the address you signed up with, and we'll delete the account and all its data within 30 days. Courses you published to students are removed along with it.

sections.title: Changes
paragraphs: If we change anything important here, we'll announce it on the platform before it takes effect. The date at the top shows the last update.

terms.title: Terms
terms.description: New Learn's terms of use: your account, your content and AI-generated content.
terms.intro: By using New Learn, you agree to these terms. The platform is still in beta.

sections.title: The service
paragraphs: New Learn turns an idea or a handout into an interactive lesson: a board drawn in code, explanations, questions, and a voice assistant called Nova. Teachers can publish their lessons to their students by link.

sections.title: Your account
bullets: You're responsible for your password and for everything that happens in your account.
The information you sign up with must be accurate.
Accounts are for people aged 13 or older; younger children use a parent's or the school's account.

sections.title: Your content
bullets: What you write or upload stays yours.
Only upload what you have the right to use, and you're responsible for that. If you upload a handout or a book you don't have the rights to, we'll remove it.
You give us permission to display and run the lesson for you and for the students you publish it to, and to keep copies of it so the service works.
If you see content that infringes your rights, email us the link and a description of your rights, and we'll suspend the content while we review.

sections.title: AI-generated content
bullets: Lessons written by AI may contain errors or gaps. Review them before you publish them to anyone.
We label this content on the platform as AI-generated, and we don't treat it as an authoritative source.
Nova is there to help you understand, not to replace a teacher or a source.

sections.title: Acceptable use
bullets: No harmful or misleading content, and nothing that breaks the law or violates other people's rights.
No attempts to access accounts or data that aren't yours, or to disrupt the service.
If you connect your own Claude or ChatGPT, you're responsible for what it does from your account.

sections.title: Availability
paragraphs: The platform is in beta: features may change or stop, and outages can happen. We provide the service as is, without warranties, and we try to give notice before any major change.

sections.title: Closing your account
paragraphs: You can close your account at any time by emailing us. If an account breaks these terms, we may suspend it after notifying its owner.

sections.title: Changes and contact
paragraphs: If we change the terms, we'll announce it on the platform before the changes take effect. For any question, the support page explains how to reach us.

general.a: It's free for now, while we're just starting out. If we add paid plans, we'll tell you well in advance, and whatever you've made stays yours.

general.q: How long does a lesson take to build?
general.a: 5 to 20 minutes, depending on its size. You can watch the steps as they happen, or close the page and come back to find it ready.
AI writes the explanations and questions and draws the board in code, and we check that the format is sound and the board works. The teacher is the one who reviews and publishes.
Yes. That's why every lesson starts as a draft: you can leave a note on any step and ask for a fix, and nothing reaches students until you publish it yourself.
The lesson, the step you're on, and your answers in this session only. Nova explains and answers, but grading comes from the lesson itself, not from Nova.
Yes. The lesson and the board fit small screens, and you can talk to Nova by voice with a single button.

general.q: Is the site available in other languages?
general.a: Yes. Pick a language at the top or in Settings, and Nova will talk to you in it. The lessons themselves stay in the language they were written in.

general.q: How do I delete my account?
general.a: Email us from the address you signed up with, and we'll delete the account and all its data within 30 days.

teachers.q: Do my students need an account?
teachers.a: Yes, a free account with their email. They open the course link and tap “Start course,” and their progress is saved.

teachers.q: Can I upload a handout or a book?
teachers.a: PDF, Word, images or text, up to 5 files. You need the right to use them, and the files are deleted once the lesson is built.

teachers.q: Can I connect my own Claude or ChatGPT?
teachers.a: Yes. You add the site as a connector and ask it for the lesson from your account. It only sees your drafts, and it can't publish or see your students.
